tagline: Shift a date context forward or backward by a specified number of intervals — the foundation of period-over-period comparisons

slides.title: Period-Over-Period Comparisons with DATEADD
slides.body: DATEADD shifts the current date filter context by a fixed number of intervals — days, months, quarters, or years. The result is a new set of dates from which you can calculate a measure, enabling you to compare the current period against any prior or future period. SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR is actually a special case of DATEADD(-1, YEAR).
slides.keyPoint: DATEADD(DateColumn, -1, MONTH) shifts the filter context back one month. The measure you wrap inside CALCULATE then evaluates as if the current month were the previous month — producing last month's value.

slides.title: Sample Sales Data
slides.caption: Monthly sales across three periods we want to compare
slides.note: Goal: for each month in 2024, show the same month from 2023 as 'Sales LY'. Report filter context: the user is viewing Q1 2024.

slides.title: Period-Over-Period Measures with DATEADD
slides.code:
-- Last Year (same month, prior year)
Sales LY =
CALCULATE(
    [Total Sales],
    DATEADD(DimDate[Date], -1, YEAR)
)

-- Last Month
Sales Last Month =
CALCULATE(
    [Total Sales],
    DATEADD(DimDate[Date], -1, MONTH)
)

-- Last Quarter
Sales Last Quarter =
CALCULATE(
    [Total Sales],
    DATEADD(DimDate[Date], -1, QUARTER)
)

-- Year over Year % Change
YoY % =
DIVIDE([Total Sales] - [Sales LY], [Sales LY])
slides.annotation: DATEADD returns a table of dates shifted by the specified interval. CALCULATE then evaluates [Total Sales] in the context of those shifted dates — effectively reading the prior period's data.

slides.title: Result — Sales with Prior Year Comparison
slides.caption: DATEADD shifts the filter context to produce the prior period comparison
slides.note: DATEADD(-1, YEAR) on Jan 2024 returns Jan 2023. CALCULATE([Total Sales]) then reads the Jan 2023 value — 78,000.

slides.title: DATEADD vs SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR
bullets: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(DimDate[Date]) is identical to DATEADD(DimDate[Date], -1, YEAR)
DATEADD is more flexible — you can shift by any number of any interval (days, months, quarters, years)
DATEADD(DimDate[Date], -2, QUARTER) compares against 2 quarters ago — no equivalent shorthand function exists
Both require a marked Date Table with a contiguous date range
Positive numbers shift FORWARD in time; negative numbers shift BACKWARD
slides.keyPoint: Use SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR for simple year-over-year comparisons. Use DATEADD for any other period shift — last month, last quarter, or multi-period offsets.

slides.title: PL-300 Exam — Key Facts
bullets: DATEADD requires a marked Date Table — without it, results will be BLANK or incorrect
The date range must be contiguous — gaps in the date table cause incorrect shifted periods
DATEADD(-1, YEAR) and SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR produce identical results — both are correct on the exam
DATEADD shifts the entire visible date range — in a Q1 2024 context, it returns all of Q1 2023
Common exam scenario: 'Calculate sales for the same period last year' → CALCULATE([Sales], DATEADD(Date[Date], -1, YEAR))
slides.keyPoint: DATEADD is the most flexible time-shift function. Memorise the syntax: DATEADD(DateColumn, NumberOfIntervals, YEAR|QUARTER|MONTH|DAY). Negative = back in time, positive = forward.
